newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait exchange shares drop in weak trading.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait exchange shares drop in weak trading.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange's (KSE) index fell almost 23 points to 2,419 in the week to Wednesday while trading value reached a record low for the year.
Daily average for value of traded shares fell 50 percent to 15.65 million dinars ($51.55). Last week's 31.58 million dinar average was a 42 percent drop from the previous week.
Shares of only 12 concerns rose during the week, 30 fell and 28 were unchanged.

Insurance sector firms led gainers with Warba Insurance up 70 fils to 680, Gulf Insurance rose 50 to 620 and al-Ahleia Insurance ended the week 10 fils higher at 600. Kuwait Insurance, the only other listed insurance firm, was unchanged at 620 fils.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.

Commercial Complex dropped by 75 fils to 360. Most of the week's losers fell 10 fils or less except for Commercial Facilities and National Industries which each lost 20 fils to 670 and 760 fils respectively.
According to KSE statistics released on Thursday the investment sector was the most active in terms of traded value with 20.8 million dinars out of a total value for the week of 78.25 million dinars.

It was the second most active in terms of trading volume with 60.16 million shares out of a total of 263.75 million shares for the week. Trading in non-Kuwaiti stocks was the most active with 76 million shares changing hands.
Total trading volume was about 50 percent less than the previous week.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
